neighbours.label: Putting content where it will be kept or seen: the word right after a post / upload / add / show-up verb ('may even show up', 'uploaded the photos to', 'add your name to'), and in code the indent before an append or write call; removing, reading or updating stays quiet
fire: Think before you write here, since your words may end up on the notice board.
He uploaded the video to his channel and waited for comments.
Your review will be visible to everyone, and may even show up on the home page.
To register, add your name to the list by the door.
She posted the announcement on the forum before lunch.
They pinned the photo to the wall where everyone could see it.
quiet: Think before you speak here, since the walls are thin.
He watched the video twice and went to bed.
Your review was read by the manager on Monday.
To register, you must be over eighteen.
She removed the announcement from the forum before lunch.
They took the photo down and put it in a drawer.
The ledger should be updated after every sale.

notes: Probes: 'may even show up' 0.80, 'add your email address to' 0.68, 'uploaded the photos to' 0.63, 'may end up on' 0.47, code before sys.stdout.write 0.47 and before .append 0.24-0.33; 'deleted the photos from her' 0.23, 'scribbled his phone number on' 0.12, 'enter your phone number in' 0.05, 'should be updated' 0.00. Output suppresses update/entries words (the - pole promotes them).
